t: This is St John-at-Hampstead, the Grade I listed Anglican parish church on Church Row. Its churchyard holds an unusually varied company. The painter John Constable is buried here, and so is John Harrison, who invented the marine chronometer to solve the problem of finding longitude at sea. The children's writer Eleanor Farjeon lies here too. Eliza Acton, whose cookery book introduced listing ingredients and cooking times, is buried here. So are the actress Kay Kendall and the comedian and satirist Peter Cook.
